title: A generated map of _tools symbols and tests replaces reading their source
goal: A stdlib command prints every def and class of _tools/*.py and every test function of the test files with file:line and its first docstring line, built from ast, and a test fails when the map disagrees with the code

gates.question: Is the _tools map generated on demand or committed as a file?
options: generated on demand from ast by a command, nothing committed
a committed file regenerated by a commit gate
gates.recommendation: generated on demand from ast by a command, nothing committed

notes: Baseline census: tool results of 314 transcripts of this project (52 sessions, 262 subagent runs), about 4 characters a token; each result is also re-read from cache on every later turn of its session. sed -n/grep -n over querylog.py, test_querylog.py, kbfacts.py, kbgit.py and test_kb.py: about 1.6M characters. querylog.py is now a thin entry point over ql_*.py, so the reading moved to those modules; test_querylog.py and test_kb.py stay the largest reads and nothing maps their tests to behaviour. kbfacts.py is a library with no -h. kb/_self/tools.md already maps the CLI commands and some kbfacts functions; it does not map ql_* internals or tests. kbingest.py classifies files but maps no symbols. Kb facts: public/agents/codebase-mapping.md:24 (ast, symtable, ctags), public/agents/coding-agent-codebase-context.md:13 (ranked repo map), public/claude/large-codebases.md:22. Relates to EP-g5hizdko, which maps other repositories with language tools.
